key_insight: Finite element error estimates for iterated quasi-reversibility jointly account for noise, mesh size, regularization strength, and iteration count in Laplacian data assimilation.
engineering_relevance: The analysis guides parameter selection for finite element reconstruction of fields governed by the Laplace equation from incomplete, noisy observations.
method: Discretize iterated quasi-reversibility with finite elements.
Derive error bounds explicit in all four noise and numerical parameters.
Use the bounds to design parameter choices ensuring convergence as noise vanishes.
evidence_signal: Two-dimensional numerical experiments illustrate the relevance of the derived error estimates.
watch_item: Validation is limited to a two-dimensional Laplacian problem; applicability to broader mechanics models or AI surrogates is not established.
paper_title: Study of the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method -- The Laplacian data assimilation case
